headline: Agenda lists $750,000 Bicentennial Square grant and a school drop-off traffic ordinance tabled to a December hearing.
summary: The posted document is an agenda with 50-plus items, including grant applications, police union contract funding, and a Cable franchise hearing. The only recorded outcome is that the Noyes and Cypress Streets traffic ordinance was tabled.
decisions: Tabled the Noyes and Cypress Streets school drop-off ordinance for a December 14, 2026 public hearing.

## City of Concord

## City Council Meeting Minutes - Final-revised

Monday, November 9, 2026

7:00 PM

City Council Chambers

37 Green Street

Concord, NH 03301

Non-public session in accordance with RSA 91-A:3, II (b) and (c) to begin at 5:30

p.m.

2. Invocation.

3. Pledge of Allegiance.

consideration be given to adding term beginning and ending dates on City Council webpage's.

Ordinance amending the Code of Ordinances; Title II, Traffic Code; Chapter 17, Vehicles and Traffic, Article 17-6, Miscellaneous Rules, by adding Section 17-6-12, Noyes Street and Cypress Streets - Restricted Access During School Drop-Off/Pick-Up Hours; together with a communication from John F. Weaver, McLane Middleton. (Reports from the City Solicitor and the Transportation Engineer submitted). (Communication from Concord School District received)

10. Ordinance amending the Code of Ordinances, Title I, General Code; Chapter 2, Finance, by creating a new Article 2-7, Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy and Resiliency (C-PACER) District; together with a report from the Director of Special Projects and Strategic Initiatives.

11. Ordinance amending the Code of Ordinances, Title V, Administrative Code, Chapter 30, Administrative Code, Article 30-3, Boards and Commissions, Board of Ethics; together with a report from Councilor Kretovic, Rules Committee Chair.

12. Resolution authorizing the City Manager to submit an application in an amount of $750,000, and to accept and appropriate Community Development Block Grant proceeds in the sum of $750,000, to support Families in Transition’s Bicentennial Square Capital Improvement project; together with a report from the Assistant Director of Community Development.

13. Resolution adopting an Anti-Displacement and Relocation Policy Statement and Procedures in support of the City’s Community Development Block Grant application to the New Hampshire Community Development Finance Authority to support Families in Transition's Bicentennial Square Capital Improvement Project at 9 Odd Fellows Avenue and 5 Market Lane; together with a report from the Assistant Director of Community Development.

14. Resolution authorizing the City Manager to submit an application in an amount of $230,000, and to accept and appropriate Community Development Block Grant proceeds of $230,000, to support Boys & Girls Club of Central & Northern NH’s Mary Stuart Gile Early Learning Center Playground project; together with a report from the Assistant Director of Community Development.

15. Resolution adopting an Anti-Displacement and Relocation Policy Statement and Procedures in support of the City’s Community Development Block Grant application to the New Hampshire Community Development Finance Authority to support the Boys & Girls Club of Central and Northern New Hampshire's Mary Stuart Gile Early Learning Center Playground Project located on the campus of the NH Technical Institute at 21 College Drive; together with a report from the Assistant Director of Community Development.

16. Resolution appropriating the sum of $22,888, to assist the Library’s mission in

providing a variety of services to patrons and accepting the sum of $22,888, in donations from the Concord Public Library Foundation (CPLF) for this purpose; together with a report from the Library Director.

17. Resolution appropriating the sum of $39,058, to fund an amendment to the Concord Police Patrolmen’s Association (CPPA) Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) and authorizing the use of $39,058, from the Human Resources Reserve for this purpose; together with a report from the City Solicitor's Office.

18. Resolution appropriating the sum of $35,682, to fund an amendment to the Concord Police Supervisor’s Association (CPSA) Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) and authorizing the use of $35,682, from the Human Resources Reserve for this purpose; together with a report from the City Solicitor's Office.

19. Public Hearing regarding the status of the $500,000, in Community Development

Block Grant (CDBG) Housing funds, the majority of which was sub-granted to Families in Transition (FIT) for the renovation of office space into 4 housing units for low and moderate income households; together with a report from the Assistant Director of Community Development.

From the City Manager

20. Positive Citizen Comments.

Consent Reports

21. Diminimus gifts and donations report from the Human Services Director requesting

authorization to accept monetary gift totaling $751, as provided under the pre-authorization granted by City Council.

22. Diminimus gifts and donations report from the Library Director requesting

Pond Hockey Association.

38. Resolution proclaiming December 2026 as Capital Region Food Program Month

(for presentation in December).

39. Resolution authorizing the City Manager to submit an application to the New

Hampshire Department of Environmental Services and Department of Business and Economic Affairs "Recharge the Adventure NH" grant program (for potential Level 2 EV charging infrastructure); together with a report from the Assistant Director of Community Development.

40. Resolution authorizing the City Manager to submit an application to the Mapillary

Camera Grant Program 3.0, and, if awarded, accept the camera equipment and execute all documents associated therewith; together with a report from the GIS Coordinator. (Pulled from consent by Councilor Davie.)

42. Resolution authorizing the City Manager to submit an application to the Stanton

K-9 Foundation grant program for up to $55,000.00, designated for Law Enforcement K-9 programs; together with a report from the Acting Deputy Police Chief.

43. Resolution repurposing the sum of $264,378.45 to include $114,378.45 from the Fire Department EMS Equipment Replacement project (CIP #527) and $150,000.00 from the New Central Fire Station project (CIP #594) for the purchase of PFAS-free boots, cabinet gear dryers, replacement of the central station SCBA compressor, purchase of patient transport ventilators, and additional funds to complete the Knox Key Secure project (CIP #671).

Appointments
